//: Strawberry. Agronomic entries are scoped by deviceNamePattern to placeholders (%strawberry%) — rename devices to match or replace the pattern with deviceProfiles before trusting an alert. Thresholds are the published extension figures cited in each entry; they are starting points, not calibrations.
//months: activeMonths are California coastal timing (fruiting spring through fall; frost risk December–March).
//enabled: Enabled: checks whose threshold is a published figure the sensor measures directly — air, leaf and soil temperature, humidity, durations, rates, pH. Disabled: checks whose threshold depends on this soil or this probe (volumetric moisture, EC, N, the 'wet' cut-off of a leaf-wetness sensor) or that need the forecast block — each says what to set before enabling it.

checks.//: ═══ FLEET HEALTH — every pack carries these, so the pack runs on its own. None needs crop tuning. ═══

═══ FREEZE ═══ Penn State: open blossoms are killed at −1.1 °C (30 °F); tight buds tolerate −5.6 °C (22 °F). Start frost-protection sprinklers at 1.1 °C (34 °F) measured at plant level and run them until the ice melts. Source: Penn State, "Frost and freeze damage on berry crops", https://extension.psu.edu/frost-and-freeze-damage-on-berry-crops
The action threshold. leaf.temperature is first because the figure is at plant level; a canopy-height air sensor reads warmer than the flowers on a clear night.
FROST TONIGHT at the sprinkler-start temperature. DISABLED: needs the top-level forecast block and a Weatherbit key (see README, Forecast).

═══ GRAY MOLD ═══ Botrytis flower infection needs ≥ 4 h of wetness at 15–22 °C (Bulger et al. 1987, the basis of the Florida Strawberry Advisory System, which reports an infection index: < 0.50 low, 0.50–0.70 moderate, ≥ 0.70 high). The index is not computed here. Sources: Bulger et al., Phytopathology 77:1225, https://www.apsnet.org/publications/phytopathology/backissues/Documents/1987Articles/Phyto77n08_1225.PDF ; NCSU, https://ipm.ces.ncsu.edu/development-of-anthacnose-and-botrytis-strawberry-fruit-infection-risk-models/
RH ≥ 90 % as the wetness proxy, as in the grape botrytis entry.
The same rule on a leaf-wetness sensor, which measures the thing the model is about. DISABLED: 50 % is a placeholder for this sensor's wet cut-off.

ROOT-ZONE SALINITY — strawberry — the most salt-sensitive crop in these packs: Maas–Hoffman threshold ECe 1.0 dS/m, above which yield declines. DISABLED until converted to what the probe reads. Maas–Hoffman thresholds are saturated-paste ECe. A soil probe reports bulk EC (or pore EC), which is not ECe: FAO 29 gives soil-water EC ≈ 2 × ECe at field capacity, and bulk EC is lower than pore EC and moves with water content. Convert before enabling — take a saturated-paste lab sample beside the probe and scale this threshold by the probe/ECe ratio. Source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29, ch. 2 and Annex 1 (Maas & Grattan 1999), https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e02.htm , https://www.fao.org/4/y4263e/y4263e0e.htm

SOIL pH — strawberry: outside 5.5–6.5. pH moves over seasons, not hours, so this is info and needs a day sustained; it stays open until the field is limed or acidified. Source: Wisconsin A2809, https://cropsandsoils.extension.wisc.edu/nutrient-application-guidelines-for-field-vegetable-and-fruit-crops-in-wisconsin-a2809/soil-ph-and-lime-requirement/
